target_customer: Local restaurants and grocery shoppers (sells through Harris Teeter and its own storefront) within about 100 miles of its farm
problem: Restaurants and consumers wanted consistent, high quality fresh greens grown nearby, without weather, pesticides or long shipping.
business_model: Grows and sells produce directly: wholesale to restaurants and grocers plus a retail storefront; technology developed in house to cut labor

founders.name: Mike Ross
prior_employers: Consulting for Fortune 100 companies and federal agencies, building enterprise software (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Georgia Tech Alumni (2019) says he worked part time at the Institute for Electronics and Nanotechnology and was encouraged to start a business.

founders.name: Jack Ross
founders.background_notes: YC page and UVA coverage describe the brothers as the founders; UVA i.Lab supported the startup before YC.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom machinery and automation for growing greens indoors involves robotics, plant science and controlled environment engineering with energy cost trade offs.

defensibility.rationale: Beanstalk claims proprietary hydroponic technology but vertical farming had many funded rivals and produce is a commodity; no patent or contract moat was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows any rival copying or buying Beanstalk; industry peers later failed or restructured, such as Bowery ceasing operations in November 2024 and AeroFarms's 2023 bankruptcy (search results, not about Beanstalk).

market_need_then: Demand for local produce and a restaurant's need for consistent salad led the brothers to build the farm (YC description); TechCrunch Demo Day coverage (2018-03-20) says it aimed to grow produce at roughly the cost of outdoor farming.

identity.visual_style: Heirloom produce and public storefront and tours planned
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly local farming story about two brothers

branding.brand_signature: Jack and the Beanstalk pun with a .farm domain

brand_strength.rationale: UVA, Georgia Tech and local press tell a brothers story and the name evokes growth, but no sourced evidence of brand driven sales; a UVA headline plays on 'Jack and His Beanstalk'.

outcome_analysis: Beanstalk started in Charlottesville as a way to supply a local restaurant with salad, went through UVA i.Lab and YC in 2018 and later moved to Northern Virginia, receiving a $200,000 state and county grant in 2021 as it expanded a Herndon farm. It sells to Harris Teeter. It remains active, but disclosed capital is small and indoor farming peers have struggled, so its long term economics are unclear.
notes: Competitors list is empty: no source dated near March 2018 naming Beanstalk's rivals was opened (TechCrunch, UVA and Georgia Tech coverage name none, and one business news page was unreachable in this session). Funding is partial: Seedtable lists the March 2018 seed with no amount, CB Insights adds Foundation Capital and i.Lab at UVA without dates, and trackers show unmatched small figures ($150K 2020, $240K total) that are unverified. Location conflicts: YC says Washington DC, other sources say Charlottesville, Springfield and Herndon, Virginia. No Beanstalk shutdown news was found.
